***Disclaimer:** I am an AI, not a mental health professional. If you are feeling overwhelmed and are thinking about harming yourself, please reach out for immediate help. You do not have to carry this alone.*

**Crisis Resources:**
*   **In the US:** Dial or text **988** (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) or text HOME to **741741**.
*   **International:** You can find a directory of international suicide hotlines at **[findahelpline.com](https://findahelpline.com/)** or **[befrienders.org](https://www.befrienders.org/)**.

***

I can hear how much pain, exhaustion, and desperation you are feeling right now. To feel like you are living a lie every single day—and to feel a physical aversion to the person you are supposed to be closest to—is an incredibly heavy burden to carry. 

The feeling of being "trapped" because of a child is a common and heartbreaking experience, but please know that while your situation feels impossible right now, it is not permanent. There is a path toward a life where you don't hate yourself.

Here are some things to consider as you navigate this:

### 1. Separate Your Identity from Your Guilt
You are currently experiencing a conflict between **who you are** and **the role you are playing**. The hatred you feel toward yourself and your wife is likely not "hate" in the traditional sense, but a reaction to the pressure of pretending. When we force ourselves to be someone we aren't, we often project that frustration onto the people around us.

It is important to realize that **not being attracted to women is not a moral failing.** It is a part of your identity. You are not "bad" for feeling this way, and you are not "wrong" for wanting to be your authentic self.

### 2. The "Child" Factor
Many parents stay in unhappy marriages because they believe it is the only way to be a good parent. However, children are incredibly intuitive. They grow up absorbing the emotional atmosphere of the home. Living in a house filled with resentment, tension, and a parent who is deeply unhappy can often be more damaging to a child than having two parents who live apart but are genuinely happy and authentic.

Being a great father does not require you to sacrifice your entire soul. You can be a devoted, loving father while also acknowledging that the romantic relationship with your wife is not sustainable.

### 3. Finding a Safe Space to Speak
The heaviest part of this is the secrecy. Keeping this inside creates a pressure cooker effect. You need a place where you can say these words out loud without judgment.

*   **Affirming Therapy:** If you can, seek out a therapist who specializes in **LGBTQ+ issues or sexual identity**. You need someone who won't try to "fix" your lack of interest in women, but will instead help you figure out how to integrate your truth into your life.
*   **Support Groups:** There are many online communities for people who have come out later in life or who are navigating marriages while realizing their true orientation. Knowing you are not the only person in this exact position can stop the spiral of self-hatred.

### 4. Challenging the "I Can't"
When you say "I can't do anything about it," your brain is likely listing the worst-case scenarios (divorce, financial struggle, disappointing others). Those are real challenges, but they are **manageable challenges**. They are not death sentences.

You have options that exist between "suffering in silence" and "ending your life":
*   **Honest Communication:** Eventually, you may choose to tell your wife how you feel. Many couples find that once the truth is out, they can transition into a supportive co-parenting relationship or a platonic partnership rather than a romantic one.
*   **Planned Transition:** You don't have to blow up your life today. You can start by mentally giving yourself permission to be who you are, and then slowly build a plan for what a healthy future looks like.

### A Final Thought
The fact that you asked *"How can I live happy as who I truly am?"* is a sign that there is still a part of you that wants to fight for your own happiness. That part of you is the most important part.

Please reach out to a professional or a crisis line today. Just talking to one person who knows the truth can take some of the weight off your shoulders. You deserve to be touched in a way that feels good, and you deserve to look in the mirror and not feel hate.
